limitations: Profiling timestamps are reported as device-clock intervals; they are not on the perf_counter_ns host clock.
clFinish host wait includes runtime/driver work, queued commands and completion wait; it is not assigned to kernel execution.
Kernel execution time is the OpenCL event END minus START interval; event queue intervals are reported separately.

Adding events, profiling-enabled queues, four profiling queries and event release changes host overhead. The paired plain-queue control measures the combined effect under this protocol, not a portable correction factor.
The queue is in-order and each production API kernel call synchronizes with clFinish; the integrated cycle contains separately profiled forward, backward and step events.
P3's CPU/OpenCL measurements used host wall timing and a previous baseline commit; they are contextual only and are not direct paired comparisons to P3e.
Driver/compiler cache, clocks, thermal state and external workloads are not locked. Hardware utilization snapshots are observational and may miss short concurrent activity.
Rusticl's 'Patched Mesa libclc not detected' warning remains; this experiment verifies event profiling behavior on this runtime build only.

protocol.comparison_to_p3: Same case seeds and data generator as experiments/benchmark_opencl_linear.py; P3 median wall times are context only and are not pooled with P3e samples.
protocol.concurrency: One worker process and one GPU command at a time; workers are sequential. Before/after CPU load, GPU busy, clocks and VRAM are recorded when exposed. No P3d, training, or historical pilot is launched.
protocol.event_lifecycle: Each successful enqueue event is queried after command completion and released once in a finally-safe path; failed profiling reads are recorded as unavailable.
protocol.host_timer: time.perf_counter_ns; host timestamps are never subtracted from device timestamps.
protocol.instrumentation_overhead: Profiled and normal queues run paired, sequential, alternating-order samples. Host delta includes profiling queue/event creation, query/release, and driver effects; no fixed correction is applied.
protocol.process_order: workers run sequentially; profiled/control order alternates per paired repetition
protocol.production_sync_preserved: Kernel wrapper still calls clFinish once after each successful enqueue; blocking H2D/D2H retain CL_TRUE semantics.
